headings: PEDD & TriNav- Device Business with Potential for Growth:
Overcoming Barriers to Effective Drug Delivery with PEDD
Treatment of Liver Tumors with Transarterial Radioembolization ("TARE")
Treatment of Liver Tumors with Transarterial Chemoembolization ("TACE")
Market Opportunity for Investigational Therapeutic Nelitolimod
paragraphs: Unless the context indicates otherwise, references in this Annual Report to the "Company," "TriSalus," "we," "us," "our" and similar terms refer to TriSalus Life Sciences, Inc. (f/k/a MedTech Acquisition Corp.), a Delaware corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries.

We are a growing, oncology focused medical technology business seeking to transform outcomes for patients with solid tumors by integrating our innovative delivery technology with standard-of-care therapies, and with our investigational immunotherapeutic, nelitolimod, a class C Toll-like receptor 9 ("TRL9") agonist, for a range of different therapeutic and technology applications. Our ultimate goal is to transform the treatment paradigm for patients battling solid tumors. We have developed an innovative technology designed to overcome two of the most significant challenges that prevent optimal delivery and performance of therapeutics in these difficult-to-treat diseases: (i) high intratumoral pressure caused by tumor growth and collapsed vasculature restricting the delivery of oncology therapeutics and (ii) off target delivery. Nelitolimod, specifically, combined with our technology aims to address the immunosuppressive properties of tumor immune cells in liver, pancreas and other solid tumors. By systematically addressing these barriers, we aim to improve response to therapies and to enable improved patient outcomes.

Many solid tumors, especially desmoplastic tumors like pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma ("PDAC"), liver tumors and various other tumor types have high interstitial fluid pressure which creates a physical barrier preventing therapeutics from penetrating the tumor. Beyond penetration issues, the blood vessels that supply these tumors are leaky and disorganized, leading to poor distribution of the therapeutic within the tumor.

We have developed a platform approach to address the unique challenges of drug delivery to solid tumors with the goal of overcoming the primary barriers described above that limit therapeutic delivery and inhibits treatment success.

Our delivery method, Pressure-Enabled Drug Delivery ("PEDD"), modulates pressure and flow within blood vessels to improve intravascular therapeutic delivery into tumors thereby increasing the likelihood of tumor response in comparison to conventional delivery technologies. Our on-market, 510(k) cleared device, the TriNav Infusion System ("TriNav") using PEDD technology is currently being used for interventional radiology procedures, most commonly transarterial radioembolization ("TARE") and transarterial chemoembolization ("TACE") in patients with primary liver cancer or in patients with liver metastases. TriNav is a highly innovative device with a novel (PEDD) delivery method. At the core of the TriNav system is SmartValve technology, a self-expanding mechanism that:
•Modulates pressure and flow of the vasculature feeding the tumor to physiologically open collapsed blood vessels,
•Creates consistent turbulent flow to promote more uniform and repeatable distribution of particles or drugs,
•Self-centers the catheter tip within the vessel for precise delivery.
This design represents a meaningful departure from traditional end-hole catheter designs by actively controlling flow dynamics and positioning to improve therapeutic outcomes.

It is U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA")-cleared and has undergone peer-reviewed studies at multiple clinical sites. The PEDD method has now been used in over 31,000 procedures, primarily TACE and TARE. TriNav achieved $45.2 million in revenue in 2025 representing growth of 53.4% vs. the previous year.

Additionally, our PEDD technology has proven to demonstrate improved drug delivery in a range of other non-malignant tumor embolizations such as Thyroid Artery embolization for treatment of Multi-nodular goiters, uterine artery embolization ("UAE") for treatment of fibroid tumors, prostate embolization for treatment of prostate cancer and an emerging new application for treatment of osteoarthritis and genicular artery embolization.

These tumor types share common procedural and drug delivery challenges as oncologic embolization such as tortuosity and small caliber target vessels, variable floor and collateral circulation, risk of off target embolization and the need for deeper penetration of embolic particles into the abnormal tissues. TriSalus is currently marketing our PEDD technology and generating clinical data in thyroid embolization, uterine artery embolization, and genicular artery embolization.

We also have developed a separate 510(k) cleared device for infusions into the pancreas, Pancreatic Retrograde Venous Infusion device, ("PRVI") to treat pancreatic tumors. TriSalus developed a novel way to access the pancreas via the venous vasculature where the vessels are larger, easier to access and PRVI with its use of PEDD, is designed to address many of the limitations inherent to arterial infusions in the pancreas. The PRVI device is currently being studied in a Phase I dose escalation trial for nelitolimod delivery into pancreatic tumors that has completed enrollment. Although FDA-cleared, the PRVI device has not yet been commercialized and commercial sale is not anticipated before 2026.

We are currently studying the ability of nelitolimod, an investigational class C TLR9 agonist, to reactivate the immune system within the liver and pancreas by broadly reprogramming immune cells and reducing myeloid derived suppressor cells ("MDSCs"), cells which cause immunosuppression, to enable more durable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors ("CPIs"), thereby improving patient outcomes.

headings: Risks Related to Our Financial Condition
We have a limited operating history, have incurred significant losses since our inception and anticipate incurring increasing expenses and continuing losses for the foreseeable future.
We may not be able to generate sufficient cash to service our indebtedness or borrow additional funds pursuant to our Loan Facility.
Our business is dependent upon the continued adoption of TriNav by hospitals and physicians.
Any change to TriNav's reimbursement status that reduces our level of reimbursement could cause TriNav sales to materially decline and impede market adoption.
Increases in costs, disruption of supply or shortage of materials could harm our business.
Risks Related to Nelitolimod and Product Development
Clinical trials of our product candidates or potential product candidates may fail to produce results necessary to support regulatory clearance or authorization.
Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
We generally do not have long-term contractual commitments from our customers, and our customers may choose not to enter into new agreements with us.
We depend on our senior management team and the loss of one or more key employees or an inability to attract and retain highly skilled employees could adversely affect our business.
If we fail to promote, protect, and maintain our brand in a cost-effective manner, we may lose market share and our ability to commercialize our products and revenues will suffer.
paragraphs: Before you make a decision to buy our securities, in addition to the risks and uncertainties discussed above under "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements," you should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report, including the accompanying financial statements and related notes, and in the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations." If any of the following events or developments described as risks were to occur, either alone or taken together, our business, financial condition, results of operations and future growth prospects would likely be materially and adversely affected. In these circumstances, the market price of our securities could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial may also adversely affect our business.

We are a commercial-stage medical device and Phase I clinical-stage pharmaceutical company with a limited operating history upon which you can evaluate our business and prospects. We have incurred significant losses since inception, including net losses of $39.2 million and $30.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $330.6 million. We anticipate incurring increased sales and general and administrative expenses related to our operations for the foreseeable future. Losses will likely continue and may increase in the future as we continue to incur significant expenses related to drug development. We may find that these efforts are more expensive than we currently anticipate or that these efforts may not result in revenues, which would further increase our losses. In addition, we have limited experience and have not yet demonstrated an ability to successfully overcome many of the risks and uncertainties frequently encountered by clinical-stage pharmaceutical companies. If we are unable to achieve and/or sustain profitability, or if we are unable to achieve the growth that we expect from these efforts, it could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations. Even if we achieve profitability in the future, we may not be able to sustain profitability in subsequent periods.

Until we are able to generate significant revenues or achieve profitability through product sales, we may require substantial additional capital to finance our operations and continue development of our product candidates. We cannot be certain that such additional financing will be available on terms favorable to us, or at all, which could limit our ability to grow and jeopardize our ability to continue our business operations.

We expect to incur significant expenses and operating losses for the foreseeable future as we continue to invest in the commercialization of TriNav, and clinical trials and other development, manufacturing and regulatory activities for TriNav, nelitolimod, and our other product candidates, and discovery research and development. Until we can generate a sufficient amount of revenue, we may need to finance our operations through strategic alliance and licensing arrangements and/or public or private debt and equity financings. The amount of capital we may need may change depending on, among other things, the success of our efforts to grow revenue, our efforts to continue to effectively manage expenses, the results of our research and development and clinical trials for product candidates, and costs arising from seeking regulatory approvals. We may not succeed in raising additional funds in a timely manner. The timing of our need for additional funds will depend on many factors, which are difficult to predict or may be outside of our control, including to continue the clinical development of, and seek regulatory approval for, nelitolimod in any indication. These factors include:
•the revenue received from sales of TriNav;

paragraphs: 除非上下文另有明確指示，否則本年度報告中提及的「本公司」、「TriSalus」、「我們」、「我們」、「我們的」及類似詞彙，均指 TriSalus Life Sciences, Inc. (f/k/a MedTech Acquisition Corp.)，為一間設立於德國的公司及其合併子公司。

我們是一家成長中的、專注於腫瘤學領域的醫療科技公司，致力於透過將我們的創新給藥技術與標準療法整合，並與我們的臨牀試驗用免疫療法藥物 nelitolimod（一種 C 級 Toll-like 受體 9（"TRL9"）刺激劑）結合，來改善患有實體腫瘤患者的治療結果，並應用於多種不同的治療與技術應用。我們的最終目標是改變患有實體腫瘤患者的治療模式。我們已開發出一種創新技術，用以克服在這些難以治療的疾病中，導致治療藥物無法達到最佳給藥與表現的兩個最主要挑戰：(i) 腫瘤生長與血管塌陷所造成的高腫瘤內壓力，限制了腫瘤學治療藥物的給藥；以及 (ii) 非目標給藥。Nelitolimod 特別是與我們的技術結合，旨在解決肝臟、胰臟及其他實體腫瘤中腫瘤免疫細胞的免疫抑制特性。
許多實體腫瘤，尤其是纖維化腫瘤如胰臟導管腺癌（"PDAC"）、肝臟腫瘤以及各種其他腫瘤類型，具有高間質液體壓力，這會形成物理屏障，阻礙治療藥物穿透腫瘤。除了穿透問題，供應這些腫瘤的血管會滲漏且無組織，導致治療藥物在腫瘤內的分佈不佳。
我們已開發出一種平台方法，用以解決將藥物送達實體腫瘤的獨特挑戰，目標在於克服上述限制治療藥物送達並抑制治療成功的最主要障礙。

我們的遞送方式，壓力驅動藥物遞送（"PEDD"），調節血 vessels 內的壓力與流動，以改善藥物在腫瘤內的血管內治療遞送，從而提高腫瘤反應的機率，與傳統遞送技術相比。我們目前上市、經 510(k) 設備清單核准的設備，TriNav 預注射系統（"TriNav"），使用 PEDD 技術，目前正用於介入放射學程序，最常見的是經動脈放射栓塞（"TARE"）和經動脈化療栓塞（"TACE"）在患有原發性肝癌或肝轉移癌的患者身上。TriNav 是一種高度創新設備，具有新型（PEDD）遞送方式。TriNav 系統的核心是 SmartValve 技術，一種自擴張機制，
•調節供應腫瘤的血管壓力與流動，以生理學方式打開塌陷的血管，
•創造一致的渦流，以促進粒子或藥物更均勻且可重複的分佈，
•使導管尖端在血管內自動居中，以實現精確遞送。
此設計代表一種與傳統端孔導管設計的重大差異，透過主動控制流動動態與定位以提升治療效果。
此產品已獲得美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准，並在多個臨牀場所進行過同儕審查研究。PEDD 方法目前已應用於超過 31,000 項手術，主要為 TACE 和 TARE。TriNav 在 2025 年實現營業收入 45.2 百萬美元，較前一年成長 53.4%。
此外，我們的 PEDD 技術已證明在其他非惡性腫瘤栓塞應用中也顯示出改善的藥物遞送效果，例如用於治療多結節性甲狀腺腫的甲狀腺動脈栓塞、用於治療肌瘤腫瘤的子宮動脈栓塞（"UAE"）、用於治療前列腺癌的前列腺栓塞，以及一種正在發展中的新應用，用於治療關節炎及關節支溝動脈栓塞。
這些腫瘤類型具有與腫瘤學栓塞手術相似的程序性與藥物遞送挑戰，例如血管迂迴與目標血管細小、變動的基底與側支循環、誤栓風險以及需要將栓塞粒子深入異常組織。TriSalus 目前正在行銷我們的 PEDD 技術，並在甲狀腺栓塞、子宮動脈栓塞以及關節動脈栓塞方面產生臨牀數據。

我們也開發了一種獨立的 510(k) 認可裝置，用於胰臟的灌注，稱為胰臟逆流靜脈灌注裝置 ("PRVI")，用於治療胰臟腫瘤。TriSalus 發展出一種透過靜脈血管系統接觸胰臟的新方法，其中血管較大、較容易接觸，而 PRVI 透過 PEDD 的使用，設計用以解決胰臟動脈灌注固有的許多限制。PRVI 裝置目前正在進行一項 Phase I 劑量遞增試驗，用於將 nelitolimod 遞送至胰臟腫瘤，該試驗已完成納入。雖然已獲得 FDA 認可，但 PRVI 裝置尚未商業化，預計商業銷售將在 2026 年前不會開始。
我們目前正在研究 nelitolimod（一種 Investigational Class C TLR9 激動劑）能否在肝臟和胰臟內重新活化免疫系統，透過廣泛重編程免疫細胞並減少髓源性抑制細胞（"MDSCs"），這些細胞會導致免疫抑制，以促進對免疫檢查點抑制劑（"CPIs"）的更持久反應，從而改善患者的治療結果。

paragraphs: 2026 年 2 月 19 日，本公司與 Lake Street Capital Markets, LLC（"LSCM"），作為名單中所列經紀商（"經紀商"）的代表，簽訂了發行協議（"發行協議"），與有關本公司普通股（"普通股"）的公開發行（"發行"）事宜，發行數量為 9,756,100 股，每股票面價值為 0.0001 美元（"普通股"），發行價格為每股 4.10 美元（"發行價格"）。根據發行協議的條款，本公司亦同意經紀商有 30 天的選擇權，可購買最多 1,463,415 股普通股（"選擇權股" 以及與普通股合稱 "證券"），以覆蓋任何過度發行的情況，發行價格扣除經紀商折扣及佣金後的價格。
2026 年 2 月 23 日，發行完成，結果發行了普通股，淨所得約為 37.0 百萬美元。發行完成後，經紀商購入選擇權股，導致額外淨所得約為 5.6 百萬美元。

headings: 與我們財務狀況相關的風險
我們的營運歷史有限，自成立以來已產生重大虧損，並預期未來一段時間內支出將持續增加且虧損情況持續存在。
我們可能無法產生足夠現金以償還我們的債務，或根據我們的貸款協議進一步借款。
與 TriNav 相關的風險
我們的業務依賴於 TriNav 繼續被醫院及醫師採用。
若 TriNav 的報銷狀態發生變動，導致我們的報銷金額降低，可能會使 TriNav 的銷售額大幅下降，並阻礙市場採用。
成本增加、供應中斷或材料短缺可能會對我們的業務造成損害。
與 Nelitolimod 及產品開發相關的風險
我們產品候選藥物或潛在產品候選藥物的臨牀試驗可能無法產生支持監管審批或授權所需的結果。
與我們業務及產業相關的風險
我們通常不會與客戶簽訂長期契約，且客戶可能選擇不與我們簽訂新的協議。
我們依賴高階管理團隊，若失去一名或多名關鍵員工，或無法吸引並留住高技能員工，可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
若我們無法以成本效益的方式促進、保護及維護我們的品牌，我們可能失去市場佔有率，且我們商品化產品的能力及營收將受到影響。
paragraphs: 在您決定購買我們證券之前，除了上述「向前看陳述的警示」段落所討論的風險與不確定性外，您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告中所有其他資訊，包括隨附的財務報表及其附註，以及「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」段落。若下列所描述的任何事件或發展發生，無論單獨或共同發生，均可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與未來成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。在這種情況下，我們證券的市場價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。

本公司為一家商業階段醫療器材及一期臨牀階段藥物公司，截至目前為止，尚無足夠的營運歷史可供評估本公司業務與前景。自成立以來，本公司已產生顯著虧損，包括截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日年度的淨虧損分別為39.2 百萬美元及30.0 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為330.6 百萬美元。本公司預期在可預見的未來，與營運相關的銷售及一般及行政費用將增加。虧損可能持續且未來可能增加，因本公司持續產生與藥物開發相關的重大費用。本公司可能發現這些努力的成本高於目前預期，或這些努力可能無法產生收入，這將進一步增加本公司虧損。此外，本公司經驗有限，尚未證明能成功克服臨牀階段藥物公司常見的風險與不確定性。若本公司無法達成及/或維持獲利，或無法達成預期的成長，將對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生重大不利影響。即使本公司未來實現獲利，也可能無法在隨後期間維持獲利。
在我們能夠透過產品銷售產生重大收入或實現獲利之前，我們可能需要大量額外資金來支應營運並持續開發我們的產品候選藥物。我們無法確定是否能以對我們有利的條件或任何條件取得額外融資，這可能會限制我們的成長能力，並危及我們持續營運的能力。

我們預期在可預見的未來，將產生重大費用與營運虧損，因為我們持續投資於TriNav的商業化，以及TriNav、nelitolimod與我們其他產品候選藥物的臨牀試驗及其他開發、製造與法規活動，以及發現研究與開發。在我們能夠產生足夠收入之前，我們可能需要透過策略聯盟與授權安排，以及公開或私人債務與 equity 融資來支應營運。我們可能需要的資金數量，將取決於多種因素，包括我們努力增加收入的成功程度、我們努力有效管理費用的成效、產品候選藥物的研究與開發及臨牀試驗結果，以及尋求法規核准所產生的成本。我們可能無法及時籌措額外資金。我們需要額外資金的時間點，將取決於許多因素，這些因素難以預測，或可能超出我們的控制範圍，包括持續進行nelitolimod在任何適應症的臨牀開發，並尋求法規核准。這些因素包括：
•從TriNav銷售所獲得的收入；
•研究與開發計畫的成本與時間，包括針對其他壓力啟動藥物遞送（"PEDD"）裝置的研究與開發計畫；
